standard_prerequisites.name: Integrality criterion over an ideal: an element of an integral extension lying in the extended ideal satisfies a monic polynomial whose remaining coefficients lie in the ideal
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: the author cites Algebra, Lemma algebra-lemma-integral-integral-over-ideal at proof lines 1968-1971
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the auxiliary monic polynomial g whose coefficients below the top one lie in the ideal.

standard_prerequisites.name: Behaviour of polynomial composition with the quadratic x squared minus x modulo the ideal
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the announced shape of the reduced polynomial.

core_obligations: Observe that the square of the element minus the element belongs to the extended ideal (proof lines 1967-1968).
Apply the integrality criterion over that ideal to obtain a monic polynomial of degree d whose lower coefficients lie in the ideal and which kills the element (proof lines 1968-1971).
Substitute the quadratic into that polynomial to obtain a monic polynomial killing the element and congruent to the announced product modulo the ideal (proof lines 1971-1974).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to an element of the extended ideal (proof lines 1967-1968).
Get the auxiliary monic polynomial (proof lines 1968-1971).
Compose with the quadratic and conclude (proof lines 1971-1975).
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces, for an element of an integral extension that becomes idempotent modulo an ideal, a monic polynomial relation whose reduction modulo the ideal is a product of powers of x and x minus one, and the proof is a 9-line construction. It starts from the observation that the square of the element minus the element lies in the extended ideal, applies the integrality criterion over an ideal to obtain a monic polynomial of degree d with all other coefficients in the ideal killing that element, and then substitutes the quadratic into the variable to get the required monic polynomial whose reduction is the announced product. The construction of the auxiliary polynomial and the substitution are the two steps, and both are displayed.
